contexts.text: The waters were dried from upon the earth () = that at that time falsities did not appear.
Behold, the faces of the ground were dry () = regeneration... The faces of the ground are said to be dry, when falsities no longer appear.
Dry places (), or places where there are no waters, = where there are no truths.
Dry breasts () = affections not of truth and good.
Dry breasts = no affections, but in their stead the cupidities of perverting. AE 710:5.
He walketh through dry places, and findeth no rest = that the life of good is such to him.
The east wind dried her fruit () = the destruction of its good.
